title: Protein generation with evolutionary diffusion: sequence is all you need

nodes.text: EvoDiff is a general-purpose discrete diffusion framework that combines evolutionary-scale sequence data with the conditioning capabilities of diffusion models for controllable protein design in sequence space rather than structure space.
nodes.evidence: we introduce a general-purpose diffusion framework, EvoDiff, that combines evolutionary-scale data with the distinct conditioning capabilities of diffusion models for controllable protein generation in sequence space

nodes.text: Current state-of-the-art structure-based diffusion models (including RFdiffusion) restrict training data and generations to a small, biased subset of protein design space because structural data (~200k PDB structures) is scarce relative to billions of natural sequences.
nodes.evidence: current state-of-the-art diffusion models generate protein structures, which limits the scope of their training data and restricts generations to a small and biased subset of protein design space

nodes.text: Sequence, not structure, is the universal design space for proteins, since every protein is completely defined by its amino-acid sequence and not every protein folds into a static structure.
nodes.evidence: However, sequence, not structure, is the universal design space for proteins. Every protein is completely defined by its amino-acid sequence.

nodes.text: EvoDiff's discrete diffusion formulation is mathematically distinct from the continuous diffusion formulations previously used for protein structure design.
nodes.evidence: EvoDiff's discrete diffusion formulation is mathematically distinct from continuous diffusion formulations previously used for protein structure design

nodes.text: EvoDiff can generate proteins inaccessible to structure-based models, such as those with intrinsically disordered regions, while still designing scaffolds for functional structural motifs without explicit structural or binder information.
nodes.evidence: EvoDiff can generate proteins inaccessible to structure-based models, such as those with disordered regions, while maintaining the ability to design scaffolds for functional structural motifs

nodes.text: EvoDiff implements two discrete forward processes: order-agnostic autoregressive diffusion (OADM), which masks one amino acid per step until the sequence is fully masked, and discrete denoising diffusion probabilistic models (D3PM), which corrupt sequences via a transition matrix toward a uniform amino-acid distribution.
nodes.evidence: In order-agnostic autoregressive diffusion (EvoDiff-OADM) ... one amino acid is converted to a special mask token at each step ... In EvoDiff-D3PM, the forward process corrupts sequences by sampling mutations according to a transition matrix

nodes.text: EvoDiff sequence models were trained on 42M UniRef50 sequences using the dilated convolutional CARP architecture (38M and 640M parameters), and EvoDiff-MSA models used the MSA Transformer architecture on the OpenFold dataset with diversity-maximized subsampling.
nodes.evidence: we trained all EvoDiff sequence models on 42M sequences from UniRef50 (26) using a dilated convolutional neural network architecture introduced in the CARP protein masked language model

nodes.text: EvoDiff is described as the first generative diffusion model for protein design trained on evolutionary-scale protein sequence data.
nodes.evidence: EvoDiff is the first generative diffusion model for protein design trained on evolutionary-scale protein sequence data

nodes.text: EvoDiff-OADM reconstructs the test set more accurately than EvoDiff-D3PM variants (uniform and BLOSUM62 transition matrices), and is the only variant whose performance scales with increased model size.
nodes.evidence: EvoDiff-OADM learns to reconstruct the test set more accurately than two tested EvoDiff-D3PM variants ... EvoDiff-OADM is the only model variant where performance scales with increased model size

nodes.text: On foldability (sequence pLDDT) and self-consistency (scPerplexity), EvoDiff-OADM outperforms EvoDiff-D3PM and improves with model size, though a left-to-right autoregressive model generates slightly more structurally-plausible sequences; the 640M OADM model was selected as EvoDiff-Seq.
nodes.evidence: EvoDiff-OADM outperforms EvoDiff-D3PM and improves when increasing the model size ... a left-to-right autoregressive (LRAR) protein language model generates slightly more structurally-plausible sequences

nodes.text: EvoDiff-Seq's order-agnostic decoding offers direct, flexible conditional generation, an advantage over LRAR models, while unconditional generation from masked language models like ESM-2 produces less structurally-plausible sequences due to train/generation task mismatch.
nodes.evidence: EvoDiff-Seq offers the advantage of direct, flexible conditional generation due to its order-agnostic decoding. Unconditional generation from masked language models produces less structurally-plausible sequences because of the mismatch

nodes.text: Experimental validation showed EvoDiff-Seq unconditional generations express and fold, with four designs exhibiting circular dichroism spectra consistent with mixed alpha-helical and beta-sheet structure, and that structural metrics like pLDDT are not always strong predictors of in vitro expressibility.
nodes.evidence: Four designs ... expressed and had circular dichroism (CD) spectra consistent with mixed alpha helical and beta sheet secondary structure ... structural metrics are not always strong predictors of in vitro expressibility
